v.why: A 0->3 identity makes the deep-path conv a residual branch that is easy to optimize, the canonical strong NB201 motif.
With an input-to-output residual, extra conv depth on the inner chain trains well and adds capacity rather than optimization difficulty.
A learned sibling conv into node 3 carries the features, so pooling edge 5 costs less.
A conv on edge 5 compensates at the output node, making a pooled edge 4 nearly harmless.
Without the 0->3 bypass the pooled edge is a larger share of the output and becomes a bottleneck.
With no direct route, node 3 depends only on edges 4 and 5, so pooling one removes a large share of learned features.
Stacked 3x3s along 0->1->3 compound receptive field, and a learned consumer of node 1 raises the value of improving node 1.
A 3x3 on edge 1 already supplies spatial features to node 2, so a parallel conv on edge 2 is partly redundant.
The input-output residual pays off most when the deep path ends in a learned conv that benefits from an identity complement.
Without the direct 0->3 route, all output signal flows through node 1, so a learned conv on edge 0 matters more.
